content.model_storage_type: Use the current model when its acceptable_entities allows this queue type.

other_info_recommendations.policy: Recommended optional metadata using the UI otherInfoKeys. No runtime enum or broker validation is implied. Omit unknown keys; never copy placeholders, invent provider/queue identities or store credentials. Examples are documentation templates, not observed application usage or executable integration tests. Preserve existing metadata; no automatic key migration.

fields.provider: Verified JMS provider/product name from source or configuration.
fields.destinationName: Actual destination name resolved from source/configuration; normally matches the physical table_name. A JNDI lookup name is recorded separately.
fields.destinationType: Recommended values: queue or topic, only when verified. These are documentation conventions, not a server-enforced enum.
fields.jndiName: Verified JNDI lookup name when JNDI is used; otherwise omit.
fields.description: Known message purpose and publisher/consumer responsibility; distinguish proposals from observed behavior.

fields.queueUrl: Verified complete queue URL from configuration or authoritative queue metadata; do not construct a URL from an unverified queue name/account.
fields.queueArn: Verified queue ARN; do not invent an AWS account ID or infer an ARN from incomplete configuration.
fields.region: Verified queue region; do not substitute the application's default region without evidence.
fields.queueType: Recommended values: standard or fifo, only when verified. These are documentation conventions, not a server-enforced enum.
fields.description: Known message purpose and publisher/consumer responsibility; distinguish proposals from observed behavior.

rules: Create jms or sqs message queue entities inside the existing general_system or framework application model when its acceptable_entities permits the selected type. The schema allowlist is authoritative, including Spring Boot, Flask and other supported frameworks. These are entity storage types, not model or processor types; do not create a separate JMS/SQS model or change the parent framework merely to represent a queue.

Reuse one verified destination entity across publishers and consumers in the current model. Preserve provider/account/region identity when distinguishing destinations with the same name. Keep publisher/listener classes or functions as allowed processors of their actual framework; JmsTemplate/JmsListener/SqsListener are Spring examples, not requirements for Flask or other frameworks. A destination is an entity, not a duplicate processor.

Use entity_name for the logical destination name and table_name for the actual physical destination. Preserve verified queue URLs/ARNs in other_info; use BE_OBJECT IDs in SQL when physical names contain punctuation or collide.

Use the UI otherInfoKeys verbatim inside entity_info.other_info: JMS provider/destinationName/destinationType/jndiName/description; SQS queueUrl/queueArn/region/queueType/description. These camelCase keys are recommended descriptive metadata, not broker configuration, required fields or enforced delivery guarantees. Do not generate snake_case alternatives for new entries; existing metadata is preserved without automatic migration.
Model only verified payload fields using the selected entity data types. Unknown payload is not an invented Object or string field. Never store credentials or connection secrets in metadata.

Publish lineage uses INSERT INTO BE_OBJECT('queue_entity_id') (field) VALUES (:callerInput), or SELECT a verified processor OUTPUT field. Consume lineage uses SELECT q.field AS existing_target FROM BE_OBJECT('queue_entity_id') q on the consuming processor. Use beyond_add_transformation_by_sql; BE records lineage and does not send or receive messages.
Read the consumer type use_lookup policy and target an existing appropriate attribute or an explicitly verified handler contract. Do not invent a handler or force all message consumers to use LOOKUP.

message_publish/message_consume may label other_info.operation, but are not native transformation types. Unknown/dynamic destinations remain unresolved metadata until configuration provides an identity; do not guess a queue or cross-provider connection.
